metadata.title: The Gray Herald's Ledger
metadata.premise: A curiosity shop that commissions retrievals hires the party to find a missing apprentice, but every piece of evidence about his disappearance contradicts the last.
metadata.narrationVoice: A wry, precise antiquarian narrator who savors irony and lingers on small telling details.

beats.title: The Cabinet of Thistlewood & Co.
beats.prose: Bells of bone and brass chime as you step into a shop crammed with impossible objects: a compass that points to regret, a birdcage that hums lullabies. Madam Corvina Thistlewood, proprietor and commissioner of retrievals, wrings her hands. Her apprentice, Wick Halloway, vanished three nights ago. His diary claims he eloped. His coat was found soaked in seawater the same night. A dockhand swears he saw Wick boarding a carriage out of town at the exact hour another witness places him drowning at the pier. Something does not add up, and Corvina wants answers before her creditors or the watch come sniffing.
beats.readAloud: "Everyone agrees on when he vanished," Corvina says. "No one agrees on how. Find the truth in the contradiction, and find my apprentice."

options.label: Examine Wick's desk for clues
Question Madam Corvina directly
Head to the docks where Wick was last seen

beats.title: A Cluttered Desk
beats.prose: Wick's desk is a jumble of receipt stubs, half-finished sketches of relics, and a diary bookmarked at an entry describing a secret elopement. Yet the ink of that entry is fresher than the pages around it, as if written after the fact.

options.label: Read the diary aloud, entry by entry
Search for a hidden compartment beneath the desk
Go ask Corvina why the ink looks so new

beats.title: The Shopkeeper's Unease
beats.prose: Corvina's fingers drum against a locked ledger. She admits the shop's rarer stock arrives through suppliers she'd rather not name, and that Wick had grown curious about them lately — perhaps too curious.

options.label: Press her about a pawned ring found in Wick's things
Ask about the shop's mysterious suppliers
Excuse yourself to inspect the docks

beats.title: Salt and Contradiction
beats.prose: Wick's coat lies snagged on a piling, soaked through with brine, though the night he vanished was dry and moonlit. A dockhand insists he watched Wick board an outbound carriage at the very hour the harbor-master logs him falling into the water.

options.label: Track footprints in the wet sand
Ask the dockhand to describe the carriage in detail
Return to the shop to examine Wick's workshop

beats.title: The Cracked Mirror
beats.prose: Behind a curtain in the back room sits a cracked mirror, its surface still faintly warm. A residue of shimmering dust clings to the frame — the unmistakable signature of a glamour, the kind that can conjure a false double to be seen in two places at once.

options.label: Study the cracked mirror fragment
Pocket a shard of the mirror for later
Head to the docks to compare notes

beats.title: Threads That Do Not Match
beats.prose: You lay the clues side by side: the too-fresh diary entry, the dry-night soaked coat, the mirror still warm with glamour. Whoever hid Wick's trail wanted every version of events to be technically true — and technically impossible.

options.label: Lay out the contradictions before Corvina
Head straight for the old lighthouse where the ring's boats dock
Dig deeper at the docks before moving on

beats.title: A Shopkeeper Cornered
beats.prose: Corvina's composure cracks. She owed the smugglers of the sunken Gray Herald a debt she could not pay in coin, so she paid it in silence — and let a glamour double cover for Wick's disappearance while they held him as leverage.

options.label: Persuade her to help you rescue Wick
Confront her with proof of the smuggling ring
Give her an ultimatum and walk out

beats.title: The Old Lighthouse
beats.prose: The disused lighthouse looms over a rocky cove, its lamp dark but its base lit from within by lantern-glow. Rope ladders and crates mark it as the smugglers' den — and Wick's likely prison.

options.label: Storm the front door
Sneak in through the sea cave
Use Corvina's leverage to negotiate

beats.title: Through the Sea Cave
beats.prose: Cold water laps your boots as you creep through a tunnel beneath the lighthouse. Ahead, a lantern-lit cellar holds crates stamped with the Gray Herald's seal — and, chained to a post, a very much alive and very confused Wick Halloway.

options.label: Free Wick immediately and slip away
Search the tower for evidence of the wider ring first
Signal the rest of the party to storm the tower now

beats.title: Terms at the Threshold
beats.prose: A smuggler broker steps out to parley, flanked by armed guards. "Corvina sent you," he says flatly. "Then Corvina knows the price of her silence."

options.label: Offer payment for Wick's release
Threaten to expose the smugglers to the watch
Trick the broker into releasing him quietly

beats.title: Guards at the Gate
beats.prose: Steel rasps from scabbards as the lighthouse's guards spot you. There is no more talking to be done — only the door ahead, and the fight to reach it.

beats.title: The Broker's Last Stand
beats.prose: Inside the lamp-room, the smuggling broker draws a curved blade, his bandits fanning out around crates of stolen relics. Wick huddles against the far wall, watching to see if his rescue was real this time.

beats.title: A Rescue Unseen
beats.prose: No alarm ever sounds. You slip away with Wick through the sea cave, leaving the smugglers none the wiser. Corvina weeps with relief when you return him, and quietly begins repaying her debt in ways that don't involve apprentices as collateral. The contradiction in the evidence, it turns out, was simply a lie well told — and you told a better one.

beats.title: The Price of Silence
beats.prose: Coin changes hands, and Wick is returned, shaken but unharmed. The smugglers vanish into the night with their crates and their secrets intact. Corvina's shop survives, though you suspect this will not be the last retrieval this arrangement demands of you.

beats.title: The Gray Herald Exposed
beats.prose: Steel or ultimatum, the smuggling ring falls apart before you. Wick is freed, the watch is summoned, and the Gray Herald's stolen cargo is seized. Corvina's shop earns a reputation for retrievals that end in justice rather than compromise — and so, it seems, do you.

beats.title: Two Prisoners Now
beats.prose: The fight turns against you, and the smugglers bind your hands alongside Wick's. Perhaps another retrieval crew will come looking someday — assuming Corvina can afford to hire one after this. The contradiction in the evidence remains unsolved, filed away with the rest of the shop's unclaimed curiosities.

victory.description: The party pushes past the smugglers' guards to reach the lighthouse's inner door before the alarm bell tolls.
